_about: Copy to repository.json and describe YOUR repository. Every field except those starting with an underscore is sent to the model with every issue, so describe the codebase and what a pull request to it can and cannot change, not your business, customers or suppliers. 'deploy_includes' is a policy choice: list only what really happens on its own when merged code is deployed. Anything not listed counts as a manual step outside the repository. Leave it empty if a deploy ships code and nothing else.
name: webapp
contains: The web application: pages, components and client-side logic
Server-side API routes and request handlers
Background job code (the job definitions and handlers)
Email and notification code (message copy stored in the database is not here)
Tests, build configuration and developer documentation
does_not_contain: Settings in third-party dashboards: payments, hosting, authentication, error tracking, email delivery
Production data, and manual one-off data corrections
Content managed outside the repository: CMS pages, copy stored in a database
Infrastructure managed elsewhere: DNS, cloud accounts, separately deployed services
Operational tasks done by hand: account changes, reports run by hand
deploy_includes: Database migrations, which run automatically on deploy
